rows: Read every item from a paginated REST API, one page per batch

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Read all items from a paginated JSON REST API at `base_url` and return them as rows `(id, name, category, price)`. Pages are requested `page_size` at a time (named argument, default 100) and streamed to DuckDB as they arrive. If a DuckDB secret of type `lidar_api` exists its `token` is sent as a bearer token; otherwise the `LIDAR_API_TOKEN` environment variable is used. Rate-limit (429) and server errors are retried with backoff.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## fetch_items(base_url, page_size := 100)

Every item from a paginated REST API, streamed one page per batch.

Authenticate with a `lidar_api` secret or the `LIDAR_API_TOKEN` environment variable:

```sql
CREATE SECRET (TYPE lidar_api, TOKEN 'your-token');
```

rows: Generate count rows of (n, squared), stepping n by step

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Generate a deterministic table of `count` rows with columns `n` and `squared`, where `n` runs `0, step, 2*step, ...`. `count` is positional (0 to 1,000,000); `step` is a named argument that defaults to 1, for example `sequence_table(5, step := 2)`. Rows stream back in batches, so large counts do not buffer in memory.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## sequence_table(count, step := 1)

`count` rows of `(n, squared)` with `n = 0, step, 2*step, ...`.

Deterministic, so it is handy for tests and demos.

rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Three rows stepping by two", "sql": "SELECT n, squared FROM lidar.examples.sequence_table(3, step := 2) ORDER BY n", "expected_result": [[0, 0], [2, 4], [4, 16]]}, {"description": "Count the rows generated", "sql": "SELECT count(*) AS rows FROM lidar.examples.sequence_table(1000)", "expected_result": [[1000]]}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "n", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "The generated value: row index times step."}, {"name": "squared", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "n multiplied by itself."}]

rows: Estimate building and canopy heights from classified LAS/LAZ points

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Read classified LAS/LAZ point clouds to estimate building and canopy heights above nearby classified ground, and find vegetation points within a three-dimensional clearance distance of supplied power-line geometry. Inputs and outputs retain caller feature IDs; horizontal coordinates and elevations must be metres. This worker uses existing ASPRS classifications: ground=2, vegetation=3/4/5, buildings=6. Height normalization uses the nearest classified ground return within ground_radius_m; sparse ground is explicitly counted. No automatic classification or vertical datum correction is implied. Missing classes give NULL percentiles. Canopy cover uses observed cells with complete ground support; observation and ground-support coverage are reported separately. Output rows stream in batches of at most 4096.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## Building and canopy metrics

Read classified LAS/LAZ point clouds to estimate building and canopy heights above nearby classified ground, and find vegetation points within a three-dimensional clearance distance of supplied power-line geometry. Inputs and outputs retain caller feature IDs; horizontal coordinates and elevations must be metres. This worker uses existing ASPRS classifications: ground=2, vegetation=3/4/5, buildings=6. Height normalization uses the nearest classified ground return within ground_radius_m; sparse ground is explicitly counted. No automatic classification or vertical datum correction is implied. Missing classes give NULL percentiles. Canopy cover uses observed cells with complete ground support; observation and ground-support coverage are reported separately. Output rows stream in batches of at most 4096.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Estimate heights above a known flat ground surface", "sql": "SELECT feature_id, round(building_p95_m, 1), canopy_max_m FROM lidar.main.height_metrics((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input())) ORDER BY feature_id"}, {"description": "Run height_metrics twice over the bundled site, at the default 2 m and at a 15 m canopy threshold, and join the results: canopy cover is 0.077 and 0.038, so half of the canopy cells hold vegetation at least 15 m tall", "sql": "WITH any_canopy AS (SELECT feature_id, canopy_cover_fraction AS cover_2m FROM lidar.main.height_metrics((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input()))), tall AS (SELECT feature_id, canopy_cover_fraction AS cover_15m FROM lidar.main.height_metrics((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input()), canopy_height_m := 15)) SELECT feature_id, round(cover_2m, 3) AS cover_2m, round(cover_15m, 3) AS cover_15m, round(cover_15m / cover_2m, 2) AS tall_share FROM any_canopy JOIN tall USING (feature_id) ORDER BY feature_id"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Building and canopy metrics on bundled synthetic data", "sql": "SELECT feature_id, round(building_p95_m, 1), canopy_max_m FROM lidar.main.height_metrics((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input())) ORDER BY feature_id", "expected_result": [["site", 11.9, 18.0]]}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "feature_id", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Caller-owned polygon identity."}, {"name": "point_count", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Number of non-noise points inside the polygon."}, {"name": "building_points", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Class-6 points with nearby classified ground support."}, {"name": "building_p95_m", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "95th percentile building height above nearest classified ground, metres."}, {"name": "building_max_m", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Maximum supported building height above nearest ground, metres."}, {"name": "vegetation_points", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Class-3/4/5 points with nearby classified ground support."}, {"name": "canopy_p95_m", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "95th percentile supported vegetation height above ground, metres."}, {"name": "canopy_max_m", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Maximum supported vegetation height above ground, metres."}, {"name": "canopy_cover_fraction", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Fraction of fully ground-supported observed cells containing vegetation above canopy_height_m."}, {"name": "observed_cell_fraction", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Fraction of polygon-intersecting grid cells with at least one usable point."}, {"name": "ground_supported_cell_fraction", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Share of observed cells whose points all have ground support; denominator for canopy coverage."}, {"name": "unsupported_points", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Building/vegetation points without ground within ground_radius_m."}, {"name": "status", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "ok, partial_ground, no_ground, or no_points."}, {"name": "cloud_crs", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Projected metre CRS of the source cloud."}]

WITH any_canopy AS (SELECT feature_id, canopy_cover_fraction AS cover_2m FROM lidar.main.height_metrics((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input()))), tall AS (SELECT feature_id, canopy_cover_fraction AS cover_15m FROM lidar.main.height_metrics((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input()), canopy_height_m := 15)) SELECT feature_id, round(cover_2m, 3) AS cover_2m, round(cover_15m, 3) AS cover_15m, round(cover_15m / cover_2m, 2) AS tall_share FROM any_canopy JOIN tall USING (feature_id) ORDER BY feature_id
Find classified vegetation within a 3D power-line clearance distance

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Compare classified vegetation returns with supplied 3D LineString/MultiLineString conductor geometry. Return exact Euclidean distance, nearest conductor coordinate and original point index for each return within clearance_m. Input conductor Z and cloud Z must share a vertical datum and metre units. Two-dimensional lines fail. An empty result means no observed encroachments, not a certified safe corridor.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## Vegetation conductor clearance

Compare classified vegetation returns with supplied 3D LineString/MultiLineString conductor geometry. Return exact Euclidean distance, nearest conductor coordinate and original point index for each return within clearance_m. Input conductor Z and cloud Z must share a vertical datum and metre units. Two-dimensional lines fail. An empty result means no observed encroachments, not a certified safe corridor.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Find a tree return two metres below a conductor", "sql": "SELECT feature_id, round(clearance_m, 2) FROM lidar.main.vegetation_clearance((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input(kind := 'conductor'))) ORDER BY feature_id, point_index"}, {"description": "Span vegetation report: join canopy height and cover from height_metrics over the right-of-way polygon with vegetation_clearance returns along the conductor (12 m search); Span 7 has 18 m canopy, one return within 3 m, two within 12 m, the closest at 2 m", "sql": "WITH spans(span_id, corridor_id, conductor_id) AS (VALUES ('Span 7', 'site', 'line')), canopy AS (SELECT feature_id, canopy_max_m, canopy_cover_fraction FROM lidar.main.height_metrics((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input()))), returns AS (SELECT feature_id, count(*) FILTER (WHERE clearance_m <= 3) AS within_3m, count(*) AS within_12m, min(clearance_m) AS closest_m FROM lidar.main.vegetation_clearance((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input(kind := 'conductor')), clearance_m := 12) GROUP BY feature_id) SELECT s.span_id, c.canopy_max_m, round(c.canopy_cover_fraction, 3) AS canopy_cover, coalesce(r.within_3m, 0) AS within_3m, coalesce(r.within_12m, 0) AS within_12m, round(r.closest_m, 2) AS closest_m FROM spans s JOIN canopy c ON c.feature_id = s.corridor_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.feature_id = s.conductor_id ORDER BY s.span_id"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Vegetation conductor clearance on bundled synthetic data", "sql": "SELECT feature_id, round(clearance_m, 2) FROM lidar.main.vegetation_clearance((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input(kind := 'conductor'))) ORDER BY feature_id, point_index", "expected_result": [["line", 2.0]]}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "feature_id", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Caller-owned conductor identity."}, {"name": "point_index", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Zero-based original point-cloud record index."}, {"name": "clearance_m", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Exact Euclidean 3D distance from vegetation return to the nearest conductor segment, metres."}, {"name": "x", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Vegetation return X in cloud_crs."}, {"name": "y", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Vegetation return Y in cloud_crs."}, {"name": "z_m", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Vegetation return elevation in metres in the supplied vertical datum."}, {"name": "nearest_x", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Nearest conductor position X in cloud_crs."}, {"name": "nearest_y", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Nearest conductor position Y in cloud_crs."}, {"name": "nearest_z_m", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Nearest conductor elevation, metres in the same vertical datum as the cloud."}, {"name": "cloud_crs", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Projected metre CRS for XY coordinates."}]
rows.vgi.title: Vegetation conductor clearance

WITH spans(span_id, corridor_id, conductor_id) AS (VALUES ('Span 7', 'site', 'line')), canopy AS (SELECT feature_id, canopy_max_m, canopy_cover_fraction FROM lidar.main.height_metrics((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input()))), returns AS (SELECT feature_id, count(*) FILTER (WHERE clearance_m <= 3) AS within_3m, count(*) AS within_12m, min(clearance_m) AS closest_m FROM lidar.main.vegetation_clearance((SELECT * FROM lidar.main.demo_input(kind := 'conductor')), clearance_m := 12) GROUP BY feature_id) SELECT s.span_id, c.canopy_max_m, round(c.canopy_cover_fraction, 3) AS canopy_cover, coalesce(r.within_3m, 0) AS within_3m, coalesce(r.within_12m, 0) AS within_12m, round(r.closest_m, 2) AS closest_m FROM spans s JOIN canopy c ON c.feature_id = s.corridor_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.feature_id = s.conductor_id ORDER BY s.span_id
